newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan should permit wrap accounts -- panel expert.
newsitem.headline: Japan should permit wrap accounts -- panel expert.

text.p: Japan should allow securities houses to use a wrap account system in order to offer new financial products to their customers, a key member of an advisory panel to the Finance Minister said on Tuesday.

"The introduction of wrap accounts would enable (Japanese securities houses) to offer new financial products to Japanese people." Hideki Kanda, a member of the Securities and Exchange Council and a professor at Tokyo University, told a parliamentary committee.
The accounts, widely used in the United States, are currently banned under Japan's Securities and Exchange Law.
The Securities and Exchange Council is working out proposals, to be finalised by June, for the deregulation of Japan's securities markets.

The wrap account system allows a securities house to manage investors' assets based on discretionary management contracts. Investors pay commissions for a package including investment advice, stock transactions and account management services.
Japan's securities industry has been urging an end to the ban on wrap accounts as part of a broad range of securities deregulation measures.
Industry sources have been worried, however, that the Finance Ministry may not allow them because of a payoff scandal at Japan's top brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Discretionary stock management was involved in a recent scandal at Nomura, which last month admitted that two directors made payments that were funnelled to a racketeer.

Kanda also told the parliamentary committee that Japan should impose harsher penalties on illegal securities deals and expand the staff at Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).
